final_recommendation: The room converged on a UBS acquisition of Credit Suisse backed by a CHF 50 billion SNB liquidity facility, with loss-floor protection capped at documented Friday liabilities, a 2 billion escrow for post-close litigation, and a 90-day closing timeline. The statement was to be locked by 6 PM Sunday and activated at 8 PM with real-time deposit acceptance, but the meeting terminated without final operational confirmation on backup protocols and board vote timing.
minority_objections: UBS CEO initially demanded separate litigation indemnity beyond the loss-floor sequencing
AT1 rep warned of litigation risk if AT1 write-down language was ambiguous or violated contractual hierarchy
key_conflicts: UBS vs Federal Council on whether litigation costs crystallizing post-close are covered by the loss floor or remain UBS's problem
AT1 rep vs FINMA/Federal Council on whether AT1 contracts' pari passu status with equity was being violated by 'sequential' write-down language
SNB vs CS CEO on operational readiness: whether deposit acceptance could be live Sunday night or only Monday morning
key_concessions: Federal Council capped loss-floor protection at documented Friday liabilities only, excluding post-close discoveries
UBS accepted a 2 billion escrow for post-close litigation in exchange for clarity on Friday balance sheet coverage
CS CEO committed to real-time deposit acceptance Sunday night at 8:15 PM with live website counter
Federal Council added explicit language that CS litigation reserves as of Friday close are not subject to post-close restatement
red_lines: Federal Council: no blank check on taxpayer exposure; loss floor capped at 5 billion and limited to documented Friday liabilities
UBS CEO: no acquisition without board approval locked by 6 PM Sunday before statement publication
AT1 rep: no AT1 write-downs unless equity is fully depleted first, with explicit contractual hierarchy protection in public text
SNB: no facility activation without Federal Council written commitment on loss protection and zero ambiguity in Sunday statement language
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: The five-minute operational window (8:03-8:15 PM) for SNB settlement and deposit counter activation had no confirmed backup protocol despite Federal Council's demand
The risk that 'binding exclusive negotiations' language might still be read as weaker than 'definitive acquisition' by some market participants
The possibility that 500 million in Sunday-night deposit inflows might be insufficient to signal stabilization versus mere survival
downstream_risk_variables: Whether UBS board actually votes by 6 PM Sunday as promised
Whether CS operations team can execute real-time deposit acceptance at 8:15 PM without technical failure
Whether the Sunday statement's AT1 protection language is legally defensible against contractual challenge
Whether visible deposit inflows Sunday night reach the 500 million target by 10 PM
Whether post-close litigation discoveries exceed the 2 billion escrow and trigger renewed creditor conflict
uncertainty_notes: The meeting terminated without final confirmation on: (1) CS's backup liquidity protocol if SNB settlement slips past 8:03 PM; (2) exact timing and documentation of UBS board vote before 6 PM Sunday; (3) whether the live deposit counter and 500M inflow target are sufficient to stop Monday morning withdrawals; (4) operational fail-safes if any element of the 8 PM activation sequence breaks. The framework is legally and financially coherent but operationally fragile.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: FINMA R2: 'confidence recovers only if Credit Suisse simultaneously announces a merger or binding capital raise by Monday close. The facility buys us the time to execute one or the other, but the run doesn't reverse on a guarantee alone.' This drove the decision to pair the 50B facility with a UBS acquisition announcement.
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: The entire meeting converged on UBS acquisition as the solution. CS CEO R4: 'binding framework announcement Sunday evening that locks in board-level intent.' UBS CEO R6: 'UBS is acquiring Credit Suisse with 90-day closing timeline.' This became the core of the Sunday statement.
marker_evidence.government_support: Federal Council R1 committed to 5B loss-floor protection as a binding condition. SNB R1: 'I need Federal Council to commit in writing tonight to a loss-protection envelope, or we're exposed open-ended.' The 50B facility and loss floor were non-negotiable government commitments that shaped the entire rescue structure.
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client R1: 'My clients aren't staying put on a handshake. They need to see the guarantee spelled out where their bankers can read it before market open, or I'm instructing transfers to UBS or offshore by Sunday EOD.' This forced the Sunday evening statement timing and real-time deposit acceptance at 8 PM.
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 rep R2: 'If you're writing them down while equity stays whole, that's an impairment of contractual rights, and I'm warning you now: my clients sue.' Federal Council R3 responded with binding commitment: 'AT1 write-downs only after equity exhaustion.' This became explicit text in the Sunday statement.
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: AT1 rep R2 challenged the 'sequential' language as violating pari passu contracts. Federal Council R3 resolved it: 'AT1 absorbs losses only after equity is fully impaired.' This hierarchy dispute forced explicit creditor sequencing language into the term sheet and public statement.
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: UBS CEO R5 demanded litigation indemnity; AT1 rep R2 warned of lawsuits if AT1 hierarchy was violated. Federal Council R6 capped loss floor at 'documented Friday liabilities' and added R9: 'not subject to post-close restatement.' The 2B escrow and explicit litigation reserve language were direct responses to litigation risk.
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Multiple references to 'by 11 PM tonight,' '6 PM Sunday lock,' '8 PM activation,' but time pressure was acknowledged as a constraint rather than driving specific decisions. FINMA R5: 'We're out of time for vague language' set deadlines but did not force a different outcome.
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Wealth client R2: 'if it's vague, they're moving assets Sunday night regardless of your guarantee.' Federal Council R2: 'if clients run anyway, we've spent the political capital.' Monday risk was raised as a concern but the solution (Sunday 8 PM activation, real-time deposits) was driven by client flight, not Monday open per se.
